description: §6.7.7 a `<request>` body that calls a CLIENT function reaching a server function gets the full request machinery (RUNTIME, sqlEngine:"real"). `pick(id)` returns `loadUser(id)`; the body is `@userData = pick(@userId)`. On mount the fetch settles (.loading false, @userData = user 1), and changing the inferred dep @userId re-fetches user 2 ("b"). Pre-S444 the settle machine was built only for a DIRECT server-fn call: the cell received an unawaited Promise at module init, .loading stuck true, and no dep effect existed. (S479: `pick` handles its call, `return loadUser(id) !{ _ :> not };` — `loadUser` is server-placed by its query and `pick` is client-placed by its `<request>` caller, so the call is a client call to a server-placed callee, failable by §19.9.10; before S479 `pick` returned `loadUser(id)` unhandled, E-ERROR-002. `pick` keeps its `User | not` return, so it is still a plain client wrapper. The runtime half is unchanged.)
rationale: §6.7.7: "The `<request>` body calls a server function." + EC-2 "The compiler SHALL generate a sequence number per `<request>` instance."; §13.2: the author writes no asynchrony. g-request-body-client-wrapper-unawaited-one-shot (S444). §19.9.10: "A call made on the client whose callee is server-placed is a **failable call** at that site, whether or not the callee is declared `!`. It SHALL be handled exactly as a call to a `!` function (§19.4.3): with a `!{}` handler, a `match` on the result, `?` inside a `!` function (§19.5.4), or as the right-hand side of a `<request>` body's assignment (§19.4.3 item 5, §6.7.7). An unhandled one SHALL be **E-ERROR-002**." (g-conf-request-body-client-wrapper-unhandled-call-s479.)
